dialogue.t: Oh, you're here! I was just starting to wonder if I should send you clearer instructions...
But then I thought, if I make my hints too obvious, it might get in the way of your travel plans...
And then, just as I was pacing back and forth, agonizing over what I was going to do... you turned up here anyway! So, it looks like everything worked out fine!
Hey, Nicole! You're so full of energy today! And... words... you're so full of words...
I'll take that as a compliment! Alright then, are you ready to check out my next room?
What the—!? Paimon almost had a heart attack, being sucked in by a painting like that! ...Wait a sec, this place looks familiar... Oh, it's the table where the mages hold their tea parties!
It all started the first time Alice invited me for tea...
On that day, I didn't attend in person — mostly because, back then, I still hadn't decided whether I really wanted to join the Hexenzirkel or not.
Alice was the only one there who knew my true identity. She warned me not to say a word, or let anyone else discover who I was. I was only supposed to observe.
...And then what happened?
Well... Then, I concluded that she was punishing me for my hesitation to join.
Everyone was talking about such interesting things. How could I not chime in?
And of course, when you're in the middle of a conversation, and someone throws out a question you know the answer to, how are you supposed to keep your mouth shut?
Which brings us to the bet between Barbeloth and Alice, Rhinedottir's forbidden creations, Ivanovna's political machinations...
It was like a series of exquisitely acted plays, distilled within the confines of a teacup. Their words alone were enough to ignite my instinct to lay the truth bare before them!
So, you piped up inside their heads?

Of course not! Even though I felt like my head was going to explode, I still made sure to hold it all in. I'm a responsible angel, after all — and I'm well aware of the difference between "what I want to say" and "what I'm allowed to say."
So I had a private little word with Alice inside her head — just me and her — and I agreed to join the Hexenzirkel, right there and then.

She was quite happy about my decision, but as for the talking inside her head... Well, she claims that over the next few days, she had such a headache that she had to visit a doctor in Liyue to get some relief. But she can hardly blame me for that!
Is that an Irminsul tree?
Oh, this painting here? You're clearly no strangers to the white trees... but did you know that the first angel's betrayal happened beneath one of their very boughs?
Huh, Paimon's curious now!
Well then, I guess it's finally time for me to tell you a tale of romance and horror. Let me just think how best to protect the identity of those involved... Alright, got it!
A long, long time ago, there was once a traveler who wandered among the stars. They were nothing like you... but that's not important right now.
One day, he traveled to a silver tree to visit the Princess of the Morning Star. Before long, he started asking her about her kingdom's most forbidden secrets.
His words puzzled the princess. How could he possibly know of all these things forbidden by the gods?
The young man revealed his origins and showed the princess things she had never seen before — of free will and love, both noble and spiritual.
His words awakened her sense of self, hitherto shackled by the gods. Her heart soared, carrying her beyond limits she had never crossed before...
The Princess of the Morning Star confided the kingdom's secrets to the youth, and between them, love grew and blossomed — along with a determination to defy the gods.
This is just a cookie-cutter love story! You said there'd be horror...
Don't worry, Paimon, the horror's about to begin. They yearned to help the people live lives of unfettered freedom, but the gods could not forgive their betrayal.
They sent down thunder and fury, destroying the lovers' home. And when the great war subsided, the power and the wisdom of the princess were lost, never to return...
Even her closest friends were cursed...
...Uhhh, yeah... That ending was pretty scary, after all...
But didn't you say you were going to tell us about the first angel? And, and... you're not saying this story's actually true, are you...?
It sure is, and that's the scariest part.
Well then, I guess it's finally time for me to tell you a tale of romance and horror.
Let me just think how best to protect the identity of those involved...
Alright, got it!
Hey, this is Simulanka! Uhm... but why are there light novels from Yae Publishing House all over the floor?
Well, on the subject of my literary enlightenment, my greatest inspiration of all... is none other than Lady Anya herself.
She was the last to join the Hexenzirkel, and yet the first to leave...
I loved all of her stories. Whether it was just an idea or a fully fleshed-out manuscript, Anya was always so skilled at making her readers gasp with joy.

Hexenzirkel discussions rarely stray far from magic, and it's my belief that Anya possessed a unique magic of her own. She could weave love and compassion into words and stories that would touch the hearts of others.
I asked her for tips on how to write compelling tales. She taught me a lot of tricks and techniques, but in the end, my biggest enemy has always been myself.

dialogue.sit: Too lazy to put pen to paper?

dialogue.t: Haha! That's one way of putting it. Communicating through thought is so much more convenient. I guess even angels can succumb to laziness.
However, recently I've resolved to make an effort, even if it's just to spare myself reproaches from a certain old Seelie friend of mine.
Ooh! Does that mean we're finally gonna get to read something you've written?
Who said anything about writing? I'm talking about buying popular works from the last few centuries to flip through in my spare time.
Haha! That's one way of putting it.
Communicating through thought is so much more convenient.
I guess even angels can succumb to laziness.
These paintings all remind me of places that hold great significance in my heart. And now, the studio has been fully restored.
Alright, go ahead and claim our reward. What? Don't look at me like that! Of course, this reward is "ours."
You're not going to leave this chest unopened, are you? I can't let you leave if you do. Besides, after telling you so many stories, don't I deserve a reward of my own?
Ahem... You still haven't taken everything!
Come to think of it... this mage's lodge holds a special significance for me, too. A painting within a house, a house within a painting... worlds within worlds. Fascinating, isn't it?
